title: Believability-Weighted Decisions
hook: The loudest person in the meeting isn't always right. Sometimes they've just never done this before.
statement: In group decisions, give more weight to opinions from people with a proven track record on that topic.
explainer: Not every opinion is equal. Someone who's done it five times knows things a first-timer doesn't. Weighting by track record takes ego out of the argument and leads to better calls.
sop: Decide what makes someone believable on this topic.
Collect everyone's opinion on the decision.
Multiply each Opinion by that person's Believability Weight, openly.
If the result splits, let one named person decide.
Check the outcome later and adjust the weights.
equation_example: Opinions score 1 to 10, weights 0.1 to 1.0. Person A: 8 × 0.9 = 7.2. Person B: 9 × 0.3 = 2.7. Total 9.9, and A counts way more. Higher totals mean your most informed voices are steering. One loud unweighted voice means trouble.
question: Pick one decision this week and name whose opinion deserves the most weight, based on what they've actually done.
closing_statement: Weight opinions by track record, not volume.
caption:
Principle Nº 279: Believability-Weighted Decisions

The loudest person in the meeting isn't always right. Sometimes they've just never done this before.

In group decisions, give more weight to opinions from people with a proven track record on that topic.
